claim: Three ways to create a new base: command palette ('Bases: Create new base' or 'Bases: Insert new base'), right-click a folder in the file explorer and pick 'New base', or click 'Create new base' in the ribbon.
quote: Bases: Create new base (same folder as active file) or Bases: Insert new base (creates and embeds in current file)... Right-click your desired folder, select New base... Click 'Create new base' in the vertical ribbon menu

claim: A base can be embedded inline in a note using a ```base code fence containing filters and views, or transcluded via wikilink syntax ![[File.base]] or ![[File.base#View]] to pin a default view.
quote:
![[File.base]] or ![[File.base#View]] to specify a default view... ```base
filters:
  and:
    - file.hasTag("example")
views:
  - type: table
    name: Table
```

claim: A .base YAML file has five top-level sections: filters (global), formulas (computed properties), properties (display config), summaries (aggregations), and views (rendering definitions).
quote: filters — Global conditions applied to all views; formulas — Custom calculated properties; properties — Configuration metadata for properties; summaries — Custom aggregation formulas; views — Data rendering definitions

claim: Filters are nested logical objects using and/or/not, combining file functions like file.hasTag(), file.inFolder(), file.hasLink() with property comparisons.
quote:
filters:
  and:
    - file.hasTag("tag")
    - or:
        - file.hasTag("book")
        - file.hasLink("Textbook")
  not:
    - file.inFolder("Required Reading")

claim: Each entry under views: takes a type, name, optional limit, groupBy, per-view filters, order (column list), and summaries — these are the saved named views.
quote:
views:
  - type: table
    name: "My table"
    limit: 10
    groupBy:
      property: note.age
      direction: DESC
    filters: {...}
    order: [file.name, note.age]

claim: Bases ships four built-in view layouts: Table and Cards (added in Obsidian 1.9), plus List and Map (added in 1.10); Map requires the Maps plugin.
quote: Table — Display files as rows in a table... Cards — Display files as a grid of cards. Lets you create gallery-like views with images... List — Display files as a list with bulleted or numbered markers... Map — Display files as pins on an interactive map. Requires the Maps plugin.

claim: Views are configured by clicking the view name in the top-left and picking the arrow next to the target view, or by right-clicking; new views are added via 'Add view' in the same menu or the 'Bases: Add view' command.
quote: Click the view name in the top left. Click the right arrow next to the view you want to configure... Click the view name in the top left and select Add view

claim: Cards view configuration includes card width, an image property (accepting [[wiki]] attachments, URLs, or hex colours), and an image fit setting of cover (crop to fill) or contain (scale to fit).
quote: Cover: The image fills the card's content box. If it does not fit, the image will be cropped. Contain: The image is scaled until it fits within the card's content box. The image will not be cropped.

claim: Practical filter workflow: click 'Filters' top-right, pick 'file' from the property dropdown, choose 'has tag', then pick a tag — the base updates instantly to all notes matching that tag.
quote: Click 'Filters' in the top right of your Base... Select 'file' from the Property dropdown... Choose 'has tag' from the filter type menu... the Base will instantly update to show me all of my notes with that tag

claim: Columns are added/removed via the 'Properties' panel next to Filters by ticking checkboxes; not every property is editable inline within the table.
quote: Click 'Properties' next to Filters... Check boxes adjacent to desired properties (modified date, folder, etc.) Selected properties automatically display in your table... some properties can be edited inline in a Base, and others cannot

claim: A useful starting column set for a first table view is file.name, two or three note properties, and a temporary file.path debugging column you remove once filters are correct.
quote: For your initial table view, start with 3–5 columns: file.name, 2–3 note properties, and one debugging column like file.path (removable later)

claim: The three canonical dataset-scoping filter idioms are file.inFolder("Projects") for folder, file.hasTag("project") for tag, and a property comparison like type == "project".
quote: Folder scope: file.inFolder("Projects"); Tag scope: file.hasTag("project"); Property scope: type == "project"
